name: Emideltide (DSIP)
description: Nine-amino-acid peptide (delta sleep-inducing peptide), first found in rabbit blood in 1963

note.text: Early studies by one group reported better sleep. Double-blind studies by other groups (1987, 1992) found little or no benefit.

bullets: **Increased deep-sleep (delta) brain waves** in rabbits, rats and cats
**Acts through the opioid system** in animals, without binding opioid receptors (FDA)
**Can trigger endorphin release,** per FDA's review of animal data
**In people,** the mechanism is not established

practical.pharmacokinetics: Cleared from the blood very fast; no data for under-skin use
practical.soldAs: Not approved; FDA panel voted against compounding use
practical.sport: Not named on the 2026 list; S0 status not stated

regulatory.text: Not approved; FDA advised against 503A listing
Not in the Oct 2026 peptide policy

references: FDA, Pharmacy Compounding Advisory Committee briefing on emideltide, Jul 2026
Neuropsychobiology, Bes et al., DSIP in chronic insomnia, 1992
